stage_title: What production cars that wire this way do better — the agent's improvement list
item: A shorted MOSFET is an output stuck ON — decide what that means for each safety load (motorsport PDM practice)
note: Read 2026-09-12. The manual is silent, and definitively so: the PMU's entire output-status vocabulary is 0 OFF, 1 ACTIVE, 2 UNDERCURRENT, 3 OVERCURRENT, 7 THERMAL SHUTDOWN - every one a story about current through an output the module believes it is driving, and none of them 'commanded off and still live'. It IS inferable: each output's voltage is measured (0-16 V on the 25 A and 15 A pins, 0-20 V on the 7 A pins), so a function comparing oN.voltage against oN.active catches a shorted high-side switch - that is CK07, and it annunciates only, because the annunciator is the module that just failed. The hard kill is the master disconnect and recovery RC01 is that sentence, first, before any other step. Worth knowing and not in the row: the PMU has a built-in inertia switch that drops every output above a configurable acceleration threshold (6 G default) - which covers the crash case exactly as long as the module is alive, and a shorted FET is the case where it is not. The O5 series relay is Camden's, as the row said: BLK-023.
